# ADR-1081: Read a Codex rollout the same way a Claude transcript is read

## Status

accepted

## Context

hooks/session_lifecycle.py needs `toolsUsed` and `turnCount` for every session, Claude or Codex (ADR-1072/ADR-1073 built the Claude-only reader). A Codex rollout is JSONL like a Claude transcript, but its records are shaped differently: the file opens with `{"type": "session_meta", ...}`, not a `{"type": "assistant", ...}` record, and its tool calls are `response_item` records of payload type `function_call` or `custom_tool_call`, not `assistant` message content blocks of type `tool_use`. Reading a rollout with the Claude reader silently returns the empty result: no line contains the literal substring `"assistant"` early enough to match, or the ones that do never carry `type: "assistant"` at the top level, so `tool_sequence` and `turn_count` both come back empty on every real Codex session, defeating procedural mining exactly as it did before ADR-1072 fixed it for Claude.

## Decision

`transcript_activity` peeks a transcript's first record before reading it: `type == "session_meta"` routes to a new `infrastructure/transcript_rollout.rollout_activity`, everything else (including a file whose first line cannot be read or parsed) routes to the existing Claude reader unchanged. `rollout_activity` yields `tool_sequence` from `response_item` records whose `payload.type` is `function_call` or `custom_tool_call`, taking `payload.name` in file order, repetitions included, capped at the same `MAX_TOOL_SEQUENCE`; `turn_count` counts `response_item` records whose `payload.type` is `message` and `payload.role` is `assistant`. A malformed line or a non-object record is skipped, not raised, matching the Claude reader's degrade. Neither reader touches prompt text: a rollout's `response_item` `message` records with role `user` or `developer` (carrying, among other things, `# AGENTS.md instructions` and `<environment_context>` blocks) are read past, the same way the Claude reader already reads past non-assistant records; a future caller that needs prompt content gets its own reader.

## Consequences

Easier: a Codex SessionEnd now feeds `mine_skills` the same way a Claude one does; the shell tool surfaces as one `exec` call per invocation regardless of what its JavaScript program does, matching how `Bash` is one call regardless of the command it runs. `tests_py/infrastructure/test_transcript_activity.py` gained a pin test confirming the dispatch peek leaves every existing Claude fixture's result unchanged; `tests_py/infrastructure/test_transcript_rollout.py` covers the new reader against a 40-line anonymised rollout excerpt and a file with no `session_meta` record. Harder: every Claude transcript is now opened twice (once to peek the first record, once to read it) instead of once; measured cost is small next to the ~4.5 ms ADR-1072 measured for a single read, but it is a second `open()` per SessionEnd that did not exist before.
